thread:
Morgan: heads-up — noticed a surprising number of requests still hitting v1 even when clients send `X-Client-Version: 2`. suspect routing entropy + token-quota clamps are interacting badly.
Alex: ugh. is it reproducible? any specific customers?
Morgan: yes, small spike from a mid-market tenant on eu-west. I dumped routing decisions — looks like our version-handshake uses a 32-bit entropy hash and we cap affinity when token-quota < 10 to avoid overallocating. when both are present we end up force-falling back to v1 for ~17% of traffic.
Rachel: 17% is... higher than expected. is that the rollforward opt-in logic or the header-negotiation path?
Morgan: header-negotiation. rollforward opt-in is separate. main issue is we combine `version_signal` + `routing_entropy` into a single comparator and the quorum threshold biases toward the older route under low quota.
Sam: can you paste the comparator snippet?
Morgan: sure — here's the simplified decision table I pulled: ```json
{"version_signal": "v2", "routing_entropy": 0.17, "token_quota": 8} -> select_v1_if_entropy<0.2_and_quota<10
```
Sam: that conditional is legacy behavior from the emergency soft-fallback. we added `quota<10` to avoid high-latency v2 spikes during cold starts.
Jaya: so the safety net is now too aggressive. idea: decouple version handshake from quota clamps — keep quota-based fallback for throughput-heavy endpoints (batch endpoints) but not for low-throughput chat/generation endpoints.
Alex: +1. we should add an override mapping in the console per-route so product teams can opt out of the quota clamp. otherwise we'll be shipping inconsistent behavior across routes.
Rachel: how does telemetry look? can we tag sampled request decisions so we can chart when quota vs entropy wins?
Morgan: I already added a probe flag in the runtime. sample header `X-Routing-Probe: 1` and it emits `routing_decision_reason` with values: handshake, entropy, quota_clamp, hard_fallback. current sample shows majority decisions labeled `quota_clamp`.
Sam: let's be careful with sampling rate — we don't want perf overhead. propose 0.5% global plus 10% for canary tenants.
Jaya: console UX: add a per-route toggle labeled "prefer-latest-version" with tooltip explaining it overrides quota clamp for that route. make it visible in rollout view and show how many requests would have been affected in last 24h.
Alex: metric-wise we need a new gauge: `routing.v2_affinity_ratio` broken down by `decision_reason` and `tenant_tier`. also add an alert if v2_affinity dips > 15% below baseline after a deploy.
Rachel: rollout plan? small canary with sampling and telemetry first. then an automated probe that flips the override for routes with stable latency/cost.
Morgan: created a quick rollout checklist: 1) patch runtime to split comparator (PR ready), 2) add probe header + telemetry (runtime + observability), 3) console toggle + query in rollout UI (product + frontend), 4) canary tenants + sampling config, 5) ramp.
Sam: can we land a quick feature-flag so we avoid a big deploy? toggle behind `routing.v2_decouple_quota` flag in feature service.
Morgan: yes, will add flag and default=false. will enable for infra & a couple of canaries.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: routing-runtime:v3.14 -> infra-staging at 1713510200
sre-bot: perf smoke OK for staging (p95 latency diff: +0.3%)
Alex: once the flag is live, we'll run A/B for 24h and collect `routing_decision_reason` breakdowns and `v2_affinity_ratio`. Sam, can you prepare the alert thresholds?
Sam: on it. propose warn at -10% and critical at -20% vs baseline computed over last 7 days.
Jaya: UI copy: "Prefer latest API version (v2). Overrides quota-based fallback for this route. Use with caution if your route expects high concurrency." also add an info link to the rollout runbook.
Rachel: nice. any open risks?
Morgan: two: 1) cost delta if v2 is more expensive for some tenants — need billing signal; 2) subtle clients that rely on v1 behavior might break. both mitigated by canary and by console opt-out.
Alex: add a telemetry tag `client_behavior_change` when a request's model/schema differs after switching to v2 so we can detect regressions in downstream consumers.
Morgan: noted. will add to probe.
Sam: ETA for flag + runtime patch?
Morgan: PRs by EOD today, staging deploy in 2 hours, canary enable tomorrow morning for 3 tenants.
Alex: thanks — let's sync tomorrow after the first canary window. :thumbsup:
